nodes.title: Arogya Sanjeevani Policy Wording: Preamble, Operative Clause, Definitions
nodes.summary: This page from the SBI General Arogya Sanjeevani Policy wording includes the Preamble, which establishes the insurance contract based on the proposal and premium; the Operative Clause, detailing indemnity for hospitalization due to illness or injury, subject to policy terms, co-pay, sublimits, exclusions, and maximum liability (sum insured plus cumulative bonus); and Definitions of key terms such as Accident, Age, Any One illness, AYUSH Treatment, AYUSH Hospital (with criteria including qualified practitioners, therapy sections, operation theatre, daily records, and at least 5 in-patient beds), AYUSH Day Care Centre (with similar criteria but no in-patient services), Break in Policy, Cashless Facility, Complainant, Complaint/Grievance, Condition Precedent, and Congenital Anomaly (internal/external). It also includes company contact and regulatory details.

nodes.summary: The text is the policy wording for SBI General Insurance's Arogya Sanjeevani Policy. It begins with a preamble establishing the insurance contract and an operative clause detailing indemnification for hospitalization due to illness or injury, subject to terms, limits, and sum insured. It defines AYUSH Day Care Centre criteria and provides extensive definitions for numerous policy terms, including accident, age, illness, hospital, medical expenses, and waiting periods. The coverage section outlines in-built benefits such as hospitalization expenses (room rent, ICU, surgeon fees), other expenses (cataract, dental, plastic surgery, day care, ambulance), AYUSH treatment, cataract treatment, pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, and specified modern treatments up to 50% of sum insured.

nodes.summary: The text from SBI General Insurance Company Limited outlines covered modern treatments, Annexure-A expense categorization, Cumulative Bonus rules, waiting periods for pre-existing diseases, first 30 days, and specific conditions (24/36 months), and exclusions. Covered treatments include uterine artery embolization, balloon sinuplasty, deep brain stimulation, oral chemotherapy, immunotherapy, intra vitreal injections, robotic surgeries, stereotactic radio surgeries, bronchial thermoplasty, prostate vaporisation, IONM, and stem cell therapy for bone marrow transplant. Annexure-A lists non-covered expenses and those subsumed into room, procedure, or treatment charges. Cumulative Bonus increases 5% per claim-free year up to 50%, reduces on claims, with detailed notes on individual/floater policies, renewal, sum insured changes, and claim notification. Waiting periods cover pre-existing diseases (36 months), first 30 days (except accidents), and specific conditions (24 months for 20 conditions like benign ENT disorders, cataract, hernia; 36 months for joint replacement, osteoarthritis). Exclusions include investigation/evaluation, rest cure, obesity treatment, gender change, cosmetic surgery, hazardous sports, breach of law, excluded providers, substance abuse, health hydros, dietary supplements, refractive error, and unproven treatments.

nodes.summary: This page from SBI General Insurance Company Limited outlines waiting periods and exclusions under the policy. It specifies a 24-month waiting period for 20 listed conditions (e.g., benign ENT disorders, tonsillectomy, cataract, hernia) and a 36-month waiting period for joint replacement and age-related osteoarthritis/osteoporosis. It then details exclusions: 7.1 Investigation & Evaluation (diagnostic admissions and unrelated diagnostics); 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care (enforced bed rest, custodial care, terminal illness services); 7.3 Obesity/Weight Control (surgical treatment unless conditions met, including BMI ≥40 or ≥35 with severe co-morbidities); 7.4 Change of Gender Treatments (except as required by Transgender Persons Act, 2019); 7.5 Cosmetic or plastic Surgery (unless for reconstruction after accident, burns, cancer, or medically necessary); 7.6 Hazardous or Adventure sports (professional participation); 7.7 Breach of law (criminal intent); 7.8 Excluded Providers (except emergency stabilization); 7.9 Alcoholism, drug or substance abuse; 7.10 Treatments in health hydros, nature cure clinics, spas; 7.11 Dietary supplements (unless prescribed); 7.12 Refractive Error (less than 7.5 dioptres); and 7.13 Unproven Treatments. The page also includes company contact and registration details.

nodes.title: 7.13 Unproven Treatments:(Code- Exel16)
nodes.summary: The text outlines SBI General Insurance's Arogya Sanjeevani Policy details: a 24-month waiting period for 20 listed conditions (e.g., benign ENT disorders, tonsillectomy, hysterectomy, cataracts, hernia, piles, varicose veins, congenital anomalies) and a 36-month waiting period for joint replacement (unless accidental) and age-related osteoarthritis/osteoporosis. It lists exclusions (e.g., investigation/evaluation, rest cure, obesity surgery, gender change treatments with transgender exception, cosmetic surgery, hazardous sports, breach of law, excluded providers, alcoholism, spas, dietary supplements, refractive error <7.5 dioptres, unproven treatments, sterility/infertility, maternity except ectopic, war, nuclear/chemical/biological attacks, domiciliary/OPD, treatment outside India, pre-existing diseases with ICD codes). It defines a moratorium period of 60 continuous months after which no claim is contestable except for fraud, applicable to first sum insured and enhanced limits from enhancement date. It details claim procedures: cashless (network provider, pre-authorization, denial rights, reimbursement fallback) and reimbursement (time limits: 30 days for hospitalization/day care/pre-hospitalization, 15 days for post-hospitalization). Notification requirements: cashless (24 hours emergency, 72 hours planned), reimbursement (48 hours admission or before discharge). Required documents: claim form, ID proof, prescription, original bills, payment receipts, discharge summary.
